## 2. A note on the language of the file

The `.ra.json` file is **deliberately bilingual, and it should stay that way.**

- **English:** `riskSource`, `exposureTarget` (where no Norwegian name is registered), and
  `effectCategory`, plus every consequence and probability label. These must match the
  tenant's vocabulary manifest exactly, and the manifest is in English.
- **Norwegian:** `template.name`, `template.description`, activity names and descriptions,
  and every `event`, `cause`, `consequence` and `minimumPpe`. These are the company's own
  words and belong in the company's own language.

Resolution forgives case and runs of whitespace, and nothing else. **Do not tidy the
English strings** — including any that look misspelled. If a label in the manifest carries
a typo, the file must carry the same typo or the value resolves to nothing and the column
imports empty.

### Were the source scores inherent?

{{This matters more than the numbers. State which of the three answers was taken:

- **Re-scored as pre-control.** The source scores reflected existing controls, so they
  were re-assessed together as the hazard before any barrier.
- **Imported as-is, knowingly optimistic.** The source scores reflect the risk as
  currently controlled. They are recorded as inherent because the format has no other
  slot, and every comparison against them inherits that optimism.
- **Omitted.** Scores were left out for the assessor to set in the tool.

Then say what the evidence was — an "Eksisterende tiltak" column beside the score, a
before/after pair, consequence text assuming protection.}}

| Source column | Rows affected | Why it did not cross |

| {{Tiltak}} | {{71}} | **Crossed, but translated.** Barriers import as library references, so the source sentence chose the entry and was then discarded — the library's wording is what lands on the risk (R24). Audit trail in §9. |
| {{Restrisiko}} | {{71}} | The format cannot express a residual at all. Barriers importing does not change this: every imported barrier arrives planned, so a residual resting on one is not established (R5). |
| {{Nr}} | {{84}} | The format carries no identifiers; array order is the ordering and the tool derives its own numbering. |
| {{Risikotall}} | {{84}} | Derived by the tool from the score pair. |
| {{Ansvarlig, Frist}} | {{84}} | These belong to a project instance, not to a generic template. |

one control must be one sentence for the actions view to group it.

## 11. Importing this file

1. Save the JSON as `{{slug}}.ra.json`.
2. In the QHSE risk-assessment template manager, choose **Import** and select the file.
   Nothing is written until Import is pressed.
3. **The template arrives as Draft and unlocked, and only a locked template can be copied
   into a project.** Anyone who imports and then goes looking for it in a project will not
   find it. Lock it first.
4. **Import always creates a new template.** It never merges into an existing one, so
   re-importing the same file gives you a second copy.
5. **Every risk carrying a barrier reads as *residual not established*** until somebody
   records that the control is actually in place. That is R5 working as designed, not a
   defect: every imported barrier arrives planned. A freshly imported template shows its
   risks as questionable, and it is telling the truth.
6. {{If any vocabulary was left unresolved: "At import you will be asked about {{n}}
   terms. §5 records the decision already taken for each — reconcile to match, or the
   register will disagree with this document."}}
